paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one: a mother cries out for her daughter, and the first answer she gets is silence. Then she hears Jesus say, "I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel." Then He says, "It is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs." (Matthew 15:23-26) If that were me, I'd be checking my apron for the exit, but she stays put and keeps asking.

So what does Jesus call great? Not her words, not her nerve. He says, "O woman, your faith is great!" (Matthew 15:28) She believed even a crumb from Him was enough and kept coming when the road got hard, and that's faith, friend: trusting that Jesus is the One to bring your need to, and staying right there.

Why does that matter to you, baker? Because you will have days when you pray and it feels quiet, and I think those days are a lot like what she walked through. Her story says keep coming to Jesus, and keep trusting that a crumb from Him is plenty. He said to her, "Let it be done for you as you desire," and her daughter was healed from that very hour, and that's the kind of Lord you're bringing your needs to. (Matthew 15:28)
